html:
The Mosetén are an Indigenous people of the Alto Beni, the forested foothills of the Andes in La Paz department, Bolivia. Their language forms the small Mosetenan family together with Tsimané, spoken by their larger neighbours to the east.

They lived by farming, fishing and hunting along the Beni and its tributaries. Franciscan missionaries worked among them from the colonial period, gathering them into mission villages such as Covendo. In the 1900s settlers from the highlands moved into the Alto Beni to grow cocoa and rice, and the Mosetén became a minority on their own land. They share the Pilón Lajas reserve with the Tsimané and have a land title of their own. Their neighbours include the Tacana.
